verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents its own named API keys, each tied to a specific environment in a project, plus personal access tokens. This gives some project/environment-level scoping of the credentials an agent could use. The evidence does not show permission-level restrictions, read-only or action-limited keys, or agent-specific credential issuance. Missing for 10: fine-grained permission scopes, least-privilege role or action restrictions, agent-specific token issuance, expiry/revocation controls, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: using a named API key associated with a specific environment in a project (`secretKey`), or using a personal access token
If a single process needs to talk to more than one Trigger.dev project, environment, or preview branch, use `new TriggerClient({...})` for each target
